title: Lear's soul-catcher-on-the-moon theory

tellings.quote: The Grays were controlling the soul sucker on the moon and when you die it sucks up your soul and it gets reprocessed unless the Grays steal it.
John Lear would say that there was like a soul catcher on the moon, but he also was kind of crazy
tellings.difference: Michels tells it briefly and calls Lear 'kind of crazy'. He leaves out the Grays and soul reprocessing.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell John Lear's claim that there is a soul catcher on the Moon.

as_told.title: John Lear's soul catcher on the Moon

plain: The claim is that a machine on the Moon catches human souls when people die. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell passes on what he says he heard from John Lear, a pilot known for his UFO claims, and also names Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft. In Corbell's version, the Grays, small grey-skinned beings from UFO lore, run a "soul sucker" on the Moon that pulls up your soul when you die so it can be "reprocessed", unless the Grays steal it first. Michels brings it up more briefly in another episode, saying only that Lear spoke of "a soul catcher on the moon" and adding that Lear "also was kind of crazy". If it were true, death would not free the soul but send it to a recycling station run by alien beings.
